Author: howdoyouturnthisoff
Description: In the late 4th century, a large number of Goths, under pressure from the Huns to move westward, crossed the Danube River and entered the Eastern Roman Empire. Roman officials mismanaged the country, lacked food supplies, and oppressed and exploited the Goths, triggering a Gothic uprising. In 378, the Gothic army continued to grow in Thrace and threatened Constantinople, the capital of Eastern Rome. The Eastern Roman Emperor Valens led his army from Antioch to the Balkans and fought a decisive battle with the Goths near Adrianople on August 9, 378. The Roman army marched long distances in hot weather, formed a chaotic formation, and underestimated the strength of the Goths. The Gothic cavalry returned to the battlefield in time and launched attacks from the flanks and rear. The Roman army was surrounded and suffered a disastrous defeat. Rome suffered heavy losses. A large number of soldiers and senior officers were killed. Valens also died in the battle. This battle became an important turning point in the late Roman Empire. Rome was unable to subdue the Goths in the empire by force. The new emperor Theodosius I subsequently adopted a policy of both pacification and military use, and finally reached an agreement with the Goths in 382, ​​allowing them to settle and serve in the empire.
Title: Battle of Adrianople
